breakfast.name: Roasted Breadfruit and Fried Jackfish
instructions: Roast breadfruit over open flame until blackened
Peel and slice
Season and fry jackfish
Serve together
breakfast.description: Roasted breadfruit with fried fish — the national dish.

breakfast.name: Bakes and Saltfish
instructions: Fry dough bakes until golden
Sauté saltfish with vegetables
Serve together
breakfast.description: Fried bakes stuffed with salt cod.

breakfast.name: Roasted Breadfruit with Saltfish
ingredients: Breadfruit (whole, roasted over fire or in oven)
instructions: Roasted breadfruit is the St. Vincent breakfast staple
The breadfruit is roasted whole over fire or in the oven
The skin chars and the inside steams -- the flesh becomes soft and creamy
Cut open and served with the saltfish sauté
This is the breakfast that St. Vincentians grew up on
breakfast.description: Saint Vincent roasted breadfruit -- whole breadfruit charred over fire or in the oven until the skin is black and the interior is soft and creamy, served with saltfish sauté (salt cod with tomato, onion, and peppers). The definitive St. Vincentian breakfast.

breakfast.name: Arrowroot Porridge
ingredients: Arrowroot starch (St. Vincent is the world largest arrowroot producer)
instructions: St. Vincent is the world largest producer of arrowroot starch
Arrowroot starch: extracted from the Maranta arundinacea plant
Arrowroot porridge is the traditional infant food and breakfast
A very smooth, light porridge -- easier to digest than cornmeal
The starch thickens milk into a silky porridge
breakfast.description: Saint Vincent arrowroot porridge -- arrowroot starch (St. Vincent is the world largest producer) cooked with milk or coconut milk, sugar, and cinnamon into a silky smooth porridge. The traditional infant food and breakfast. Easier to digest than cornmeal.

lunch.name: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Boil callaloo and dasheen
Add coconut milk, meat, okra, dumplings
Simmer until thick

lunch.name: Pelau
instructions: Brown chicken with sugar
Add rice, peas, coconut milk
Cook covered until done

lunch.name: Breadfruit Oil-Down
ingredients: Coconut milk (must be rich -- the liquid)
instructions: Oil-down is the national dish of Grenada and also St. Vincent
The name: the coconut milk is cooked down until only the oil remains -- the oil rises
When done, the ingredients are coated in coconut oil that has separated from the milk
The breadfruit absorbs the coconut milk and becomes soft and flavorful
Cooked in one pot with layered ingredients
The yellow color from turmeric is the visual signature
lunch.description: Saint Vincent oil-down -- breadfruit and saltfish with callaloo leaves and dumplings cooked in coconut milk until the milk reduces to just coconut oil (the oil-down moment). The breadfruit absorbs the coconut milk flavors. Turmeric gives the yellow color. Shared national dish with Grenada.

lunch.name: Pepperpot Soup
ingredients: Cassava (or cassareep -- the concentrated cassava juice)
instructions: Pepperpot is one of the oldest indigenous American dishes still eaten today
Cassareep: the essential ingredient -- concentrated cassava juice that acts as a preservative
The Amerindians who first inhabited the islands made pepperpot with cassareep
The original pepperpot was a perpetual pot: new ingredients added daily, never fully emptied
The cassareep preserved the stew for days without refrigeration
The dark, thick stew with cassareep has a slight bitterness and deep sweetness
lunch.description: Saint Vincent pepperpot -- one of the oldest surviving indigenous Caribbean dishes, made with cassareep (concentrated cassava juice that acts as a preservative and darkens the stew), meat, and root vegetables. The Amerindian original was a perpetual pot never fully emptied; cassareep prevented spoilage.

lunch.name: Flying Fish and Cou-Cou
ingredients: Flying fish (cleaned, seasoned with lime and herbs)
Cou-cou: cornmeal cooked with okra into a firm polenta-like mold
instructions: Flying fish and cou-cou is the national dish of Barbados -- also eaten in St. Vincent
Flying fish: a small, silvery fish that glides above the ocean surface on its pectoral fins
The Eastern Caribbean flying fish season: they follow the warm currents
Cou-cou: cornmeal cooked with okra until very thick, then molded
The okra in the cou-cou gives it a slightly slimy, smooth texture
Served with the flying fish and a Creole tomato sauce
lunch.description: Eastern Caribbean flying fish and cou-cou -- flying fish (the gliding fish of Caribbean waters) served with cou-cou (cornmeal cooked with okra until thick and firm, then molded) and Creole tomato sauce. National dish of Barbados but eaten across the Eastern Caribbean including St. Vincent.

dinner.name: Stew Chicken Vincentian
instructions: Brown chicken with browning sauce
Add vegetables and spices
Simmer 25 min
Serve with rice and provisions

dinner.name: Lambi Curry
instructions: Dice conch, sauté with curry
Add coconut milk and potatoes
Simmer until tender

dinner.name: Stewed Conch
instructions: Conch stew is made from the queen conch -- the large Caribbean sea snail
The shell: a large, pink spiral shell -- used as a horn throughout the Caribbean
The meat: large, firm, and rubbery unless tenderized
Tenderization is essential: pounding or marinating in lime juice
Stewed in a tomato and coconut milk sauce until tender
dinner.description: Saint Vincent stewed conch -- queen conch meat tenderized by pounding (the shell is the large pink Caribbean spiral), then braised in tomato-coconut milk sauce with Scotch bonnet until tender. The conch shell doubles as a horn in Caribbean tradition.

dinner.name: Goat Roti
instructions: Roti is the Indian contribution to Caribbean food -- brought by indentured workers
Indian indentureship replaced slavery in the Caribbean after 1838 emancipation
The Indians brought their food traditions: roti, curry, and dhal
Goat curry roti: goat meat curried with potato, wrapped in a large roti
The roti skin is a paratha-style flatbread, brushed with oil and layered
The roti is large enough to wrap the curry inside -- it is the vessel
dinner.description: Saint Vincent goat curry roti -- goat meat curried with potato in Trinidad-style curry (strong, fragrant), wrapped inside a large paratha-style roti flatbread. Indian indentureship (post-1838 emancipation) brought roti and curry to the Caribbean; it became a staple across the Eastern Caribbean.

dinner.name: Pelau
instructions: Pelau is the one-pot rice dish common across the Caribbean
The rice, peas, and chicken all cooked together in coconut milk
Browning sauce (caramelized sugar) is added to the chicken first
The browning colors the rice deep golden-brown
Coconut milk gives the rice a creamy, fragrant quality
dinner.description: Eastern Caribbean one-pot rice -- chicken browned with caramelized sugar (browning sauce), rice and pigeon peas added with coconut milk, all cooked together until the liquid is absorbed. The browning sauce gives deep color; the coconut milk gives fragrance.

snacks.name: Arrowroot Biscuits
instructions: Cream butter and sugar
Add arrowroot flour and egg
Shape into cookies
Bake at 175°C 20 min
snacks.description: Delicate cookies from SVG's famous arrowroot.

snacks.name: Cassava Pone
instructions: Cassava pone is the Caribbean cassava cake -- dense, sweet, and chewy
Raw cassava is grated and combined with coconut and sugar
Baked until firm and golden
The texture: dense, slightly chewy, very sweet
Cassava is the indigenous Caribbean staple -- cultivated by the Arawak and Carib peoples
snacks.description: Caribbean cassava cake -- raw grated cassava combined with grated coconut, sugar, butter, and warm spices, baked until firm and golden with a dense, chewy texture. Cassava was the indigenous Arawak and Carib staple.

snacks.name: Peanut Punch
instructions: Peanut punch is the Caribbean street drink -- high protein, filling
Blended peanut butter with milk and sugar
Nutmeg is the essential spice -- always freshly grated
The Guinness version: stout mixed in -- called the Brown Cow in some islands
Sold by street vendors at carriages in St. Vincent
snacks.description: Caribbean peanut punch -- natural peanut butter blended with milk or coconut milk, sugar, vanilla, and freshly grated nutmeg into a thick, filling protein drink. The Guinness stout version adds a malt dimension. Sold by street vendor carts.

snacks.name: Sweet Potato Pone
instructions: Sweet potato pone is similar to cassava pone but with sweeter flavor
Grated sweet potato carries more natural moisture and sweetness
Combined with coconut and brown sugar
Spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger
snacks.description: Caribbean sweet potato pone -- grated sweet potato combined with coconut, brown sugar, and warm spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger), baked until firm. Sweeter and more moist than cassava pone. A Caribbean bake-sale staple.

desserts.name: Sweet Potato Pudding
instructions: Mix all ingredients
Pour into pan
Bake at 160°C 60 min

desserts.name: Coconut Roll
ingredients: Sweetened coconut filling (fresh grated coconut with sugar, spice)
instructions: Coconut roll is the sweet Caribbean bake -- rolled pastry filled with spiced coconut
A sweetened coconut filling rolled inside a simple pastry
Baked until the pastry is golden
Cut into slices -- the spiral of coconut and pastry is revealed
desserts.description: Caribbean coconut roll -- simple pastry dough rolled around a spiced sweetened coconut filling, baked until golden. Cut to reveal the spiral cross-section of pastry and coconut. A Caribbean bakery staple.

desserts.name: Black Cake (Rum Fruit Cake)
ingredients: Dried fruit: currants, raisins, prunes, cherries -- soaked in rum for weeks
instructions: Black cake is the Caribbean Christmas cake -- a dense, very dark fruit cake
The fruit is soaked in rum for weeks or months -- the longer the better
The browning sauce gives the cake its nearly black color
A dense, moist cake that is very boozy
Made weeks before Christmas and aged with rum
Every Caribbean family recipe is a closely guarded secret
desserts.description: Caribbean Christmas rum fruit cake -- dried fruit soaked in rum for weeks, combined with browning sauce (for the nearly black color) and warm spices, baked dense and moist. Aged by brushing with rum after baking. Made weeks before Christmas; every family recipe is a secret.

drinks.name: Seamoss Drink
instructions: Soak sea moss overnight, boil
Blend with milk and spices
Chill

drinks.name: Sorrel Drink
instructions: Boil sorrel with ginger and cloves
Strain, sweeten
Chill
drinks.description: Tart sorrel drink with ginger and cloves.

drinks.name: Sorrel Drink
instructions: Sorrel is the Caribbean hibiscus drink -- the Christmas drink
Not sorrel the herb -- this is dried hibiscus flowers (Hibiscus sabdariffa)
The flowers are steeped in hot water with cinnamon, cloves, and ginger
The result: a deep ruby-red drink, tart and floral
Sweetened with sugar -- served cold
The Christmas drink in the Caribbean -- made for the holiday season
Rum can be added -- the spiked version is for adults at the Christmas gathering
drinks.description: Caribbean Christmas hibiscus drink -- dried hibiscus flowers (sorrel) steeped with cinnamon, cloves, and ginger, sweetened and served cold. The deep ruby color and tart floral flavor define the Caribbean Christmas season. An unspiked version is for children; rum is added for adults.
